clue.text: Draw a drink and beam

blocks.note: port is a fortified wine from Portugal
a beam of light is a ray

explanation.surface: Someone at the bar pours a drink and smiles broadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beam' reads as a smile, but here it is a shaft of light.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray someone is to depict them, as an artist does with pencil or brush.

clue.text: Shock at rogue's twisting

indicators.note: twisting bends things out of their original shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Onlookers are scandalised by the villain's crooked dealings.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is': the rogue is twisting.
explanation.definitionFit: Outrage is a strong feeling of indignant affront, the reaction to something truly appalling.

clue.text: Tedious routine sent up in an Italian place

indicators.note: in a down entry, sending something up makes it read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a rut is a dull, unchanging routine

explanation.surface: A boring daily grind gets mocked somewhere in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent up' looks like satire; it turns the word for a tedious routine upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin is a major city in the Piedmont region of northern Italy.

clue.text: Relevant article for petty officers

blocks.note: PO is the abbreviation for a petty officer, plural POs

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece is judged pertinent to junior naval ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: Apropos means pertinent or to the point, from French for 'to the purpose'.

clue.text: Rather big girl - has to be dressed differently

indicators.note: anything put together differently is arranged in a new order

explanation.surface: A girl who has outgrown her clothes must wear something else.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffix -ish softens an adjective, so largish is somewhat sizeable, fairly substantial.

clue.text: State support in beer production

indicators.note: one thing set in another is enclosed by it

blocks.note: ale is a type of beer, the brewery's product
a leg supports a table or chair

explanation.surface: Someone declares their backing for brewing.
explanation.walkthrough: The support goes between the second and third letters of the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: To allege is to assert or declare something, typically without proof.

clue.text: A plentiful supply of excellent wood

blocks.note: deal is fir or pine timber

explanation.surface: A timber merchant boasts of plenty of top-quality wood.
explanation.walkthrough: Deal is a British term for softwood planks of pine or fir.
explanation.definitionFit: A great deal is a large amount, a phrase meaning lots of something.

clue.text: Record collection many have

blocks.note: a set is a collection of things
D is the Roman numeral 500, a large number

explanation.surface: Lots of people own a stack of vinyl records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many' standing for a Roman numeral such as D or C is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something down is to write it out in permanent form, putting it on paper.

clue.text: Defamatory reporter responsible for devastated man's cold anger

indicators.note: something devastated is wrecked, its parts thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A libellous journalist provokes a ruined man's icy fury.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandalmonger spreads malicious gossip that damages reputations, a defamer by trade.

clue.text: Make a move to provide porridge

blocks.note: second meaning: British slang for prison, where one does porridge (serves time)

explanation.surface: Getting up to make the breakfast oats.
explanation.walkthrough: Porridge is not oats here: in British slang 'doing porridge' means serving a prison sentence, and stir is also slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir means both to shift slightly from rest and, as slang, a jail where convicts serve time.

clue.text: Calls to mind resolution about rally

blocks.note: to rally troops is to gather them together

explanation.surface: A motion concerning a protest meeting is brought to mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resolution' asks for the answer to be broken into parts: about plus rally. To recollect oneself is also to summon up resolve.
explanation.definitionFit: To recollect something is to remember it, bringing a past event back into memory.

clue.text: Caught a worker retiring on the quiet to have forty winks

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the word goes backwards

blocks.note: c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
the worker ant is a crossword staple
p is piano, the musical marking for quiet

explanation.surface: An employee caught slipping off to bed on the sly for a snooze.
explanation.definitionFit: Forty winks is an idiom for a short daytime nap, the same as a brief doze.

clue.text: "Antigone" reading may be getting the thumbs-down

indicators.note: a reading is one interpretation, so the word is read another way, its letters reordered

blocks.note: the Sophocles tragedy, taken as written

explanation.surface: A staging of the Greek tragedy is panned by critics.
explanation.definitionFit: A thumbs-down is a refusal or rejection, the act of denying or saying no.

clue.text: The longest day

blocks.note: surface reading: midsummer, the day with most daylight
setter's reading: the day whose name has the most letters

explanation.surface: Midsummer, or the D-Day film of that name.
explanation.walkthrough: The solstice and the war film both mislead; 'longest' is measured in letters, and nine beats every other day of the week.
explanation.definitionFit: Of the seven weekday names, the midweek one is spelled with nine letters, more than any other.

clue.text: Greek character seen around at assembly, of course

indicators.note: something seen around another surrounds it on both sides

blocks.note: nu is the thirteenth letter of the Greek alphabet
a rally is a mass gathering

explanation.surface: A Greek is spotted at a public meeting, as you'd expect.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturally and 'of course' are both adverbs meaning as expected, obviously.

clue.text: Aims to live on!

definitions.note: a noun phrase: what one lives on

blocks.note: second meaning: income or resources one survives by

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark makes it sound like a rallying cry to endure; the second sense is a noun for income.
explanation.definitionFit: Means is both a verb for intending and a noun for the money or resources that support a person.

clue.text: A most appealing French accent

blocks.note: cute means highly attractive or charming

explanation.surface: Praising the charm of someone's Parisian way of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French accent' sounds like a way of speaking; it is the mark over é.
explanation.definitionFit: The acute is the rising diacritic mark used in French spelling, as in café.

clue.text: Some reached Dartmoor in the West Country

definitions.note: names the region the place is in rather than the place itself

indicators.note: some means only part, so just a portion of the following words is used

explanation.surface: A walker made it to the moorland in south-west England.
explanation.walkthrough: Dartmoor is a moor in Devon; the West Country is south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheddar is a village in Somerset, famous for its gorge and cheese, in south-west England.

clue.text: The bloomer of a witless push-over

indicators.note: turning something over flips it, so the preceding words read backwards

blocks.note: to ram is to push hard

explanation.surface: A blunder made by someone foolish and easily beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a mistake and 'push-over' like an easy victim; the bloomer is something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: The amaryllis is a lily-like flowering bulb, so it is something that blossoms.

clue.text: About the current height for power station equipment

blocks.note: a tor is a rocky hill

explanation.surface: Discussing electrical supply and pylon heights for a power plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear reactor is the plant in which fission produces heat to generate electricity.

clue.text: Hero-worship can make one so idle!

indicators.note: making something out of materials turns them into a new form

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Fans who adore a celebrity end up doing nothing else.
explanation.definitionFit: To idolise is to admire someone excessively, to put them on a pedestal like a deity.

clue.text: A minister's standard issue

blocks.note: par is the normal or expected level

explanation.surface: A government minister's routine announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' suggests politics, but it is a cleric; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A parson is a parish clergyman, one who ministers to a congregation.

clue.text: Fruit coming by sea, a variety of apples

blocks.note: the main is a poetic word for the open sea

explanation.surface: Produce is shipped in, including several apple types.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruit' looks like the definition but supplies the first half.
explanation.definitionFit: Pearmain is a long-established cultivar of English apple, such as the Worcester Pearmain.

clue.text: He wrote "Gold, the Endless Gold"

indicators.note: without an end means the last letter is cut off

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Crediting the writer of an adventure novel with a gold-rush title.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted title is invented; gold appears twice, once as the chemical symbol and once as the heraldic word.
explanation.definitionFit: An author is the person who wrote a book, so 'he wrote' describes the role.

clue.text: Charges could well be dropped with some sorrow

definitions.text: could well be dropped with some sorrow

blocks.clueFragment: could well be dropped with some sorrow
blocks.note: second meaning: drops shed from the eyes when weeping

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a court case where accusations are regretfully withdrawn; both senses are elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Tears is a verb for dashing at speed and a noun for drops shed in grief.

clue.text: The teenager making a scene and told off

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or awry, so the letters are out of order

explanation.surface: A youngster throws a tantrum and gets scolded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Told off' reads as scolded, but only 'off' is the signal; 'told' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An adolescent is a young person between childhood and adulthood, typically aged thirteen to nineteen.

clue.text: Blue as a result of getting a duck?

blocks.note: in cricket a duck is a score of zero

explanation.surface: A batsman is depressed after being out without scoring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' sounds like sad; it is a dye colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Anil is the indigo plant and the deep violet-tinged dye made from it.

clue.text: The old king observing a sign of advancing age

blocks.note: GR is Georgius Rex, King George
eyeing, here spelt eying, is watching

explanation.surface: An elderly monarch watches for signs that he is growing older.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair turning silver-white is a familiar visible mark of growing older.

clue.text: Journalists going before their boss get flattened!

blocks.note: the press is the body of journalists

explanation.surface: Reporters who face their editor get crushed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pressed has been squashed smooth under weight, like ironed clothes or flowers.
